items.title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
items.content: Meta and Apple have teamed up for the launch of the social media giant's newest model, Muse Spark Open, which will run locally on Apple silicon.

items.title: Spotify users on iOS 27 can now ask Siri to play music without having to say ‘on Spotify’
items.content: Siri can now learn users' preferred music app, allowing Spotify listeners to request songs, podcasts, and playlists without specifying which app to use.

items.title: Chinese hackers spied on thousands of companies after breaching IT giant ConnectWise
items.content: Microsoft points the blame for ConnectWise's breach at a China-aligned hacker, which relied on AI agents to rapidly hack into thousands of its customers.

items.title: Microsoft says AI agents are like insider threats as ‘frontier models can’t be trusted’
items.content: Microsoft wants enterprises to closely watch the agents that employees use with systems not controlled by AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic.

items.title: Microsoft president says UK is best placed to drive AI regulation
items.content: Microsoft president Brad Smith calls for urgent AI regulation, saying milk and washing machines have more oversight than AI companies.

items.title: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’
items.content: In a Saturday morning post, Microsoft's CEO wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.

items.title: What Is PHP? Why Are Government and Business Websites Going Offline?
items.content: A critical security flaw in the programming language underpinning much of the web has prompted a global rush to patch vulnerable systems.

items.title: A.I. and Its Dangers Are Embedded In the Midterm Elections
items.content: The midterms are the first elections in which artificial intelligence is integrated into every major social media platform. Efforts to blunt its harms are uneven.

items.title: Barclays to Cut 5,000 Jobs in A.I.-Driven Push to Lower Costs
items.content: The move is the latest illustration of a company saying it believes it can be more efficient with fewer workers because of artificial intelligence.
